entries.defect: CAMERA_OFFSET is the only camera placement in the material; its call site, aiming and clipping are not attached. If the pose is traveller+offset with lookAt(traveller), shifting the position alone re-aims the lens and steepens the tilt; the look target must carry the same zoom-scaled shift.

The follow camera steers toward the traveller as view centre and may derive lookAt/pitch from it; the shift must enter both the pose and the aim from the same (current or lagged) follow point, or the camera lags, overshoots, re-centres the traveller, or shows motion-dependent tilt, and the no-jump angle rule may read the shift as a heading change.

entries.file: outside material — camera init, follow updates, debug jump / teleport lerp (invariants.mjs:96 'big camera lerp')
entries.defect: Initialization, remount and teleport/jump paths independently reconstruct a traveller-centred pose (traveller+offset looking at the traveller); an unchanged path restores the old framing or ends every jump with a re-aim snap, and the verify settle waits assume the lerp ends centred.

FLORA_SPAWN_MARGIN / hard-cap comments promise a fogged, invisible streaming boundary with the plant circle centred on the traveller while fog is measured from the camera; the camera moving from 24 to ~31.5 south of the traveller eats the ~6-unit no-pop margin, so the south rim and rebuild pops can fall inside faint-fog view.

floraSpawnRadius / floraInSpawnCircle / floraShouldRebuild take the traveller as the circle centre 'beyond the visible ground'; because the shift scales with zoom, the south deficit grows at every wider zoom up to FLORA_SPAWN_HARD_CAP.

The low-preset claim that the tighter ~173 circle stays beyond the frustum at zooms <= 0.5 was argued from a traveller-centred view and must be re-derived with the frame reaching ~7.5 x zoom-scale further south.

VEGETATION_HIDE_ZOOM 2.5 is justified by FLORA_RANGE_MAX coverage measured around the traveller keeping the streaming edge out of view; the translated footprint (scaled shift ~19 units at zoom 2.5) pushes the south frame edge past that coverage before the hide threshold.

The terrain chunk window, movement prediction and nearest-first build order are centred on the traveller as the visible-region centre; moving or jumping south the newly visible south strip is built late or not at all (holes / stand-in LOD at the bottom edge) while northern terrain no longer shown is prioritised.
The LOD refine rings are centred on the traveller's chunk; the near-ring quality doubling now partly falls above the top of the picture while the south frame (up to 28 units vs ~21) gets coarser LOD.

The far-terrain sheet is skipped at zoom <= 1 on the assumption that the detailed chunk window around the traveller covers the whole frame; with more south reach the bottom edge can run off the window with no far sheet beneath it.

entries.file: src/scenes/travel/TravelScene.tsx:943 (sun / CSM, target placement outside material)
entries.defect: Shadow near/far and a light target or shadow box anchored on the traveller assume shadowed ground centred on the traveller; the cascades follow the camera but a traveller-anchored target loses south-frame shadow coverage.

nearestActors ranks by distance from camera.position as a stand-in for 'nearest the traveller/centre', and the declutter depth is measured from the camera; with the camera ~7.5 further south the 24-label cap and the nearer-name priority favour bottom-of-frame actors and drop ones beside the traveller.

entries.file: src/scenes/travel/frameVisibility.ts:1, src/scenes/travel/Wildlife.tsx:44 (seeders, scripted spawns, vicinity / dry-shore guarantees)
entries.defect: Seeders and guarantee spawns that call isOnScreen generate and count candidates in traveller-centred rings sized for the old ~21-unit south reach; with 28 units south more candidates are rejected, the offscreen guard protects insertion but not appearance, and vicinity herds / dry-shore drinkers silently under-fill or cluster north.

'The nearest water in the traveller's view' is chosen by distance from the traveller; water north beyond ~28 units is no longer in the picture, so the guarantee can fill a shore the player cannot see.

entries.file: outside material — src/scenes/travel/Wildlife.tsx (chunk windows, nearest-instance selection)
entries.defect: Ordinary wildlife chunk windows and nearest-instance render-slot selection may treat the traveller-centred population as the visible population; the visible southern strip can be underpopulated or lose render slots.

entries.file: outside material — src/scenes/travel/TravelScene.tsx (flora rebuild origins, nearest-first fill, instance caps)
entries.defect: Flora rebuild origins, nearest-first filling and instance-cap selection may rank around the traveller instead of the translated view, spending constrained buffer capacity outside the picture and leaving visible southern dressing sparse.

Flight spawn starts on a traveller-centred viewR + FLIGHT_SPAWN_OUT ring and pushes outward at most 12 steps; without the offscreen predicate distance substitutes for visibility, south-bearing spawns need more steps, and after 12 the bird spawns where it is with no final visibility guarantee.

Flight despawn uses the traveller-centred viewR ring as floor; the live isOffscreen branch still protects visible birds, but the no-predicate fallback viewR + FLIGHT_DESPAWN_OUT despawns in view on the south side.

The predator entry probe (minR..maxR, 16 bearings x 6 rings) sizes maxR for the old frame and, without the offScreen predicate, accepts the bare minR ring as outside a traveller-centred picture; for prey south of the traveller the rings can be exhausted and the truncated fallback may place the predator on screen.

The despawn ring is centred on the player; the projection backstop keeps visibility, but the ring over-retains north and under-retains south, and its sizing note (wide-zoom corner) no longer covers the south-shifted case.

The leaving predator's 'view ring' is traveller-centred; a predator walking north leaves the picture well before the ring and paces off-screen until overtime, one walking south can still be in frame when the ring is passed.

Hunt, family-drama and scavenger target eligibility use distance to the player as a visibility proxy; a calf ~20-28 north now sits at the top edge or out of frame and consumes the opportunity while newly visible southern subjects are excluded.
Vultures circle the traveller, now ~37% from the top; a circle radius sized to the old centred frame pushes the north half of the flock out of the top of the picture.
A 24-unit chase is described as 'still on screen' by world distance alone, with no projection; a chase into the formerly visible northern strip now leaves the picture.

entries.file: src/scenes/travel/TravelScene.tsx:1893 (enter hint, hint UI outside material)
entries.defect: The enter hint replaces the world-projected place label; if the hint UI is anchored at frame centre because the traveller occupied it, the replacement now sits ~13% below the traveller and settlement.

The pop-in drive holds KeyW northward and treats the camera glued to the player as the view; the check is projection-based and holds, but with the north reach shrunk the path it was calibrated on reveals spawns differently and a passing run proves less.
The dist-from-traveller in pop findings is read as distance from view centre; after the shift triage by distance misleads (25 north is at the edge, 25 south mid-lower picture).

entries.file: scripts/verify/enrichments.mjs:1435-1439 (stain staging; candidate search and clip construction truncated)
entries.defect: The stain staging picks the steepest clear patch near the traveller within a ring assumed to be in the picture; spots north of ~28 are now out of frame and are only rejected late by the existing 'projected clear of the HUD' gate, which can stage nothing.
The trample victim is injected at the player's spot and the stain shots framed on it; the stain now sits above centre, and any downstream centre-of-frame clip or cell layout (truncated) degrades.

The travel shutter subject/framing test likely uses the traveller as default subject with an NDC-near-0 or off-axis tolerance, or substitutes traveller proximity for projection; travel frames are refused or mis-graded with the traveller at NDC y ~ +0.26.
A travel framing helper that centres a requested subject by jumping the traveller onto it now puts that subject above centre; composing a shot must account for the translated optical aim.

entries.file: outside material — scripts/verify (centre crops, centre-pixel probes, screenshot clicks, baselines)
entries.defect: Fixed centre crops, centre-pixel probes, screenshot clicks and baselines intended to locate the traveller sample the wrong screen position; no travel-specific implementation is visible in the excerpts.

entries.file: outside material — follow-camera verify of the preceding point (commits 1d8fd2faa / 8c8b76ced, WebGL 2 walk frames)
entries.defect: The per-frame follow-camera angle check likely measures tilt as the camera->traveller direction or traveller at NDC 0; after the shift the measured angle changes although orientation is unchanged, so the check breaks or must use the camera's own forward vector.

Zoom scales CAMERA_OFFSET about the traveller as fixed point; with the shift also scaling, the zoom pivot is no longer the picture centre and the traveller slides vertically during a zoom unless the shift scaling matches exactly.

entries.file: outside material — map / position query (window.__camera helpers, map overlay, debug readouts)
entries.defect: Helpers that return the view centre (camera target or ground under NDC 0,0) as the traveller now differ by ~7.5 x zoom-scale units, affecting map recentre, the minimap viewport rectangle and position readouts; the gameplay position itself stays valid.

entries.file: outside material — src/scenes/travel/TravelScene.tsx (centre-ray picking, cursor steering)
entries.defect: Any centre-ray pick, cursor-steering origin or screen-to-ground shortcut that equates frame centre with the traveller position introduces a southward targeting error.

entries.file: outside material — fog (TRAVEL_FOG near/far, clearView) and near/far planes
entries.defect: Fog distances and near/far or clear-view calculations were tuned with the camera ~48 from the traveller; at ~52.5 (more with zoom) the traveller and near field sit deeper in fog, the far-north visible limit moves in, and intended subjects can be clipped or fogged.
The rain instanced volume is positioned at the traveller or camera target and sized for the old frame; the lower picture (now 28 units south) can run past the box and show a rain-free band.

entries.file: outside material — panorama capture readiness (TravelScene.tsx:1846, panoramaMath)
entries.defect: The capture gate reads the committed chunk set built around the traveller; if the chunk window is re-centred on the new view centre to fix the south strip, place chunks may not be committed when the traveller is inside the ring and the capture bakes a terrainless band — the two must change together.

A capture implementation recovering its origin from the travel camera with the old offset captures displaced scenery; the supplied TravelScene caller passes settlement coordinates explicitly, so that caller itself does not show the defect.
A positional-audio listener attached to the camera sits ~7.5 further south of the traveller; near sounds pan or attenuate as if the player stood lower in the picture.
